comments.author: eyerow
comments.story_title: ACM Prize in Computing Awarded to AlphaGo Developer
comments.why_zh: 关于 AlphaGo 对阵李世石比赛的感人纪录片
comments.text_zh: 作为一名多年的围棋爱好者和机器学习从业者，我大学时甚至还自己做过一个（虽然很烂的）围棋 AI，所以我可能有点偏见，但看 AlphaGo 对李世石的那场比赛，真的感觉像是在看我们这代人的登月。如果你们还没看过，DeepMind 在 YouTube 上做了一部新的 AlphaGo 纪录片：[VIDEO]。看得我热泪盈眶。这既是人类的胜利——我们造出了这样一台不可思议的机器，也是人类的失落——围棋那无尽的奥秘将被削弱，然后又再次是人类的胜利——李世石在第四局的精彩一胜……
comments.text: As a long-time Go player and ML guy who even built his own (albeit shitty) Go AI in college, I'm a bit biased, but watching the AlphaGo-Lee Sedol match really felt like watching our generation's moon landing. If y'all haven't already, there's a new AlphaGo documentary made by DeepMind on YT: [VIDEO] . Brought tears to my eyes. Both a triumph for humanity in building an unbelievable machine like this, and a loss for humanity in that the infinite mystery of Go will be diminished, and again a triumph for humanity in Lee Sedol's brilliant win in Game 4...

comments.text: I consider AlphaGo - The Movie [1] to be a timeless classic that will never feel outdated. In my opinion, it surpasses even Hollywood productions, despite being based on true events and filmed live with real people. I'm ranking it as #2, though, because I still believe Steve Jobs' 2007 iPhone presentation [2] is the greatest live tech event ever captured on film. Hearing the crowd screaming when seeing some tricks and techniques ( eg. slide to unlock , pinch to zoom and scrolling up ) on how to use the phone does really triggers some haptic feedback in my heart because we are now so used to these tricks that were pure magic back then. ______________________________ 1. comments.author: mwattsun
comments.why_zh: 讲述亚洲人因 AI 击败围棋冠军而震惊的故事
comments.text_zh: 《AlphaGo - The Movie》真的让我印象深刻，虽然我对围棋了解不多，但他们讲述故事的方式——亚洲国家的人们那么确信自己的冠军能在一场围棋锦标赛中战胜电脑，结果电脑赢了，他们被震得对人工智能有了全新的认识。我理解这由此引发了一场 AI 军备竞赛。编辑：完整影片在 YouTube 上免费观看：AlphaGo - The Movie | 完整获奖纪录片 [VIDEO]
comments.text: I was really impressed by "AlphaGo - The Movie", despite not knowing much about Go, because the way they told the story, people from the Asian countries were so sure their champion would win a Go tournament against a computer, that were stunned into a new consciousness about artificial intelligence when the computer won. This started an arms race in AI is what I gather. Edit: Full movie for free on YouTube: AlphaGo - The Movie | Full award-winning documentary [VIDEO]

comments.author: russellbeattie
comments.story_title: In Two Moves, AlphaGo and Lee Sedol Redefined the Future (2016)
comments.why_zh: DeepMind 制作的一小时比赛纪录片，谈到了第 37 手和第 78 手
comments.quote_zh: 我刚看完 DeepMind 制作的那部关于这场比赛的时长一小时的纪录片
comments.text_zh: 巧的是，我刚看完 DeepMind 制作的那部关于这场比赛的时长一小时的纪录片 [1]。它大量谈到那两手棋——不过并没有真正深入细节。对我这种非围棋玩家来说，第 37 手和第 78 手都显得完全随意。我的意思是，视频大部分内容都在讲，不可能像国际象棋那样算出所有后续着法，然而在一盘可能约 300 手的棋里，第 37 手被称为天才之手，第 78 手则被称为 God Hand。对我这样的外行来说，这似乎有点不一致。让我会心一笑的是历史如何重演。Sedol 预测会以 5-0 战胜这个程序。Kasparov 在 1990 年代也相当自负。你会以为总会有人警告他！“嘿，Sedol。冷静点，这些人不会花这么多钱只是为了让自己丢脸。”DeepMind 肯定比 IBM 礼貌得多，这点很好。Deep Blue 团队对 Gary 有点混蛋。 1. [VIDEO]
comments.text: Coincidentally, I just watched the hour long documentary that DeepMind made about the match [1]. It talks a lot about the two moves - though not really in detail. To a non-go player like myself, both moves 37 and 78 seemed completely arbitrary. I mean, much of the video talks about how it's impossible to calculate all the future moves like in chess, yet move 37 of a possible ~300 move game is called out as genius, and move 78 is a God Hand. For the layman like myself, it seemed a bit inconsistent. The thing that made me smile was how history repeated itself. Sedol predicted a 5-0 win against the program. Kasparov was pretty cocky as well in the 1990s. You'd think someone would have warned him! "Hey Sedol. Cool your jets, these guys wouldn't be spending so much money just to embarrass themselves." DeepMind was definitely way more polite than IBM, so that was good to see. The Deep Blue team were sorta jerks to Gary. 1. [VIDEO]
